title: Runtime Config Safety Gateway for Automated Batching & Cache Recommendations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a 'Config Safety Gateway' service that validates, simulates, and orchestrates safe application of automated batching and caching recommendations produced by the Optimize pipeline. The gateway enforces latency and throughput SLO guardrails (p50/p95/p99), installs runtime limiters during canary, and gates changes with anomaly detection signals. The aim is to enable automatic cost-saving tuning while preserving SLOs and minimizing manual rollbacks.
background: We have multiple automation efforts that propose batching profiles and cache policies (Optimize, autotune agents). Past rollouts have occasionally regressed tail latency during busy windows. Current manual canaries are slow and error-prone. We need an automated, policy-driven safety layer that can: 1) simulate expected SLO impact before applying; 2) apply changes behind limiters and gate rollout based on live telemetry; 3) automatically roll back on early anomaly signals.
proposed_solution:
Implement a standalone gateway service sitting between Optimize -> Orchestrator and the runtime. Key features:
- Pre-apply simulator: use short synthetic replay of recent traffic sample (prefix + KV distribution) to predict latency/throughput delta and cache-hit delta.
- SLO policy engine: declarative policies (e.g., max p99 increase 5ms, max throughput drop 3%) that accept/reject proposals.
- Canary limiter: create runtime scoped limiters (qps, concurrency, token-per-second) that gradually increase new profile traffic over N minutes.
- Anomaly detector: streaming detector that consumes latency, error-rate and tail-quantiles; uses rolling window and two-stage detection (threshold + statistical unexpected shift) to trigger immediate rollback.
- Safe-apply orchestration: orchestrates staged application across model variants, regions, and capacity tiers with automatic fallback to previous profile.
- Observability: detailed diff of expected vs observed token-cost, cache-hit-rate, and per-route p99 time series in Console.
Implementation notes: start with a module that can be invoked by Optimize as an external validation API, then integrate with orchestrator for apply/rollback commands.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (API + simulator): expose a REST API for Optimize to submit a proposal and receive a decision + predicted metrics. Phase 2 (Read-only canary): apply profile in 'shadow' mode to 1% of traffic using limiter without changing billing routing; collect real telemetry for 24h. Phase 3 (Staged apply): apply limiter-backed rollout (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) with automatic checks at each step. Phase 4 (Full apply + monitor): remove limiter, continue extended monitoring and mark change as completed. Each phase must have a manual abort and an automatic abort if anomaly detector trips.
rollback_plan: Two rollback types: immediate and graceful. Immediate rollback will revert to the last good profile and re-route traffic within 30s (for severe p99/regression). Graceful rollback drains new-limiter capacity and moves traffic back over 5 minutes when regression is small but persistent. All rollbacks must create an incident ticket and attach the diagnostic snapshot produced by the gateway simulator and anomaly detector.
telemetry_and_alerts: Telemetry inputs: per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, tail latency distribution, KV cache hit-rate, request concurrency, tokens/sec, error-rate, CPU/GPU utilization. Alerts: 'gateway-sim-prediction-mismatch' when observed metrics deviate > 15% from simulator prediction; 'fast-rollout-p99-spike' when p99 increases beyond policy; 'anomaly-detector-trigger' for statistical shifts. Dashboards: per-proposal panel showing predicted vs observed curves and a canary timeline view.
acceptance_criteria: Optimize can call safety-gateway API and receive deterministic accept/reject with detailed predicted delta metrics
Simulator prediction error (abs delta) for p99 under shadow workloads < 12ms for 80% of proposals in internal tests
Canary limiter increments traffic and automatically aborts if configured SLO policy breaches are detected
Anomaly detector triggers rollback within configured window in integration tests with synthetic regressions
Console shows proposal diff and per-route canary timeline; engineering runbook autogenerated for rollbacks
open_questions: Which simulator fidelity trade-offs are acceptable (sample window length vs prediction accuracy)?
Do we allow Optimize to auto-apply proposals or require PM/SE approval for P0 customers?
Should limiters be global per-model or per-route? Hybrid approach?
How to handle proposals that touch cache eviction/quantization where simulator predictions are weak?
